about.title: About
about.made: Made with love in [[Madrid]] by iDeo

story.leadBody: Lanzador Claude is the front door to Claude Code on Windows. Pick the project folder, tick how you want Claude to start and press Launch. The launcher opens the terminal in that folder with environment variables and flags already set, so there are no options to remember and no paths to type.
story.what1: Browses the whole disk from the root folder you choose (`C:\Desarrollo` by default), with recents and favourites.
story.what2: Shows every Claude Code flag and environment variable with an explanation in your language.
story.what3: Remembers the options you pin and groups them into reusable profiles.
story.what4: Creates new projects with their folder, their `CLAUDE.md` and the skills you choose.
story.what5: Lives in the system tray, can start with Windows and opens with Ctrl+Alt+I.
story.how1: There are two parts inside one program. The engine, written in Rust, reads folders, stores settings, installs skills and launches Claude in Windows Terminal, PowerShell or WSL. The interface, built with web technology, is what you see on screen.
story.how2: They talk to each other through Tauri. The indicator at the bottom left confirms the interface is connected to the engine.
story.why1: **Rust** for the engine: fast, memory-safe, and it produces a small executable that needs nothing else installed.
story.why2: **Web interface** for the visuals: it allows a polished Docker Desktop-style experience with tooltips, light and dark themes and three languages.
story.why3: **Tauri** to join them: it uses the WebView2 that Windows 11 already ships, so the installer is a few megabytes instead of the 150 of an Electron app. It includes MSI and EXE installers and signed updates.
story.origin1: The project was born in the IT Maintenance department of iDeo and is developed by the Software Development department of iDeo.
story.origin2: Its purpose is simple: to make life more pleasant for everyone who uses Claude Code.
story.origin3: It was built with *vibe coding* by the iDeo team using Claude Code, and its source code has been reviewed and refined by people using Microsoft Visual Studio.
